title: Determination of Clostridium sp. Contamination Level
author: Eva Petrova

steps.title: Resuspend sample in saline
steps.instruction: Weigh 10 g of soil sample and resuspend it in 90 mL of sterile 0.85 % NaCl saline solution.

steps.title: Prepare decimal dilutions
steps.instruction: Create a series of at least five decimal (10‑fold) dilutions of the suspension in the same saline solution according to standard guidelines.

steps.title: Inoculate TPGY broth tubes
steps.instruction: Dispense 10 mL of pre‑generated TPGY broth into each tube (one tube per dilution level for each sample). Add 1 mL of each dilution to the corresponding tube.

substeps.instruction: Number of tubes = number of samples × number of dilution levels; each tube represents a specific dilution.
Ensure thorough mixing after adding the dilution.

steps.title: Pasteurize inoculated tubes
steps.instruction: Subject the inoculated tubes to pasteurization at 70 °C for exactly 15 minutes.

steps.title: Incubate tubes anaerobically
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes under anaerobic conditions at either 30 °C or 37 °C for 48 hours.

steps.title: Assess broth turbidity and gas
steps.instruction: After incubation, examine each tube for turbidity of the TPGY broth and note any gas production.

steps.title: Plate cultures on agar
steps.instruction: Spread 10 µL of each liquid culture onto the surface of FAA agar and Willis–Hobbs agar plates.

substeps.instruction: Incubate the inoculated plates anaerobically at 37 °C for 48 hours.

steps.title: Evaluate phenotypic features
steps.instruction: After plate incubation, evaluate characteristic phenotypic features of the colonies and determine the contamination level as the highest dilution at which clostridial growth is observed.
